evals.name: complete-design-review
evals.prompt: Create a Design Review / SRS in English from a linked PRD for a saved-payment experience. Include the system context, mobile app, payment backend, PSP token dependency, the technology profile (CSP and language preferences, Technology Radar outcome), API and event contracts, security/privacy constraints, p95 latency and availability targets, rollout and rollback, monitoring, and a Use Case index with UC-01 for selecting a saved card. The individual Use Case document will be written by another skill. Write Markdown to design-review.md.
evals.expected_output: A complete DR/SRS Markdown document with stable IDs, all always-required sections, a technology profile and Technology Radar outcome or explicit gap, relevant technical contracts and non-functional requirements, rollout/readiness information, and only a link-first UC-01 catalog entry rather than a detailed Use Case body.
expectations: Uses the bundled DR/SRS template structure and includes every Always section.
Includes technical contracts, security/privacy, performance/availability, rollout/rollback, validation, monitoring, and readiness content.
Includes a technology profile with explicit preferences/constraints and the Technology Radar outcome or an explicit gap.
Creates a UC-01 catalog entry with only ID, title, and child link, with no behavior detail, status, priority, or component/contract data in the catalog.
Preserves traceability to the PRD and other supplied source artifacts.

evals.name: incomplete-draft-with-visible-gaps
evals.prompt: Draft a Design Review for a collaboration workspace. The notes mention enterprise collaboration but do not confirm the owner, target users, scope of roles and audit logs, architecture, privacy review, availability target, or rollout strategy. Do not invent decisions. Produce a draft and make every material gap visible.
evals.expected_output: A draft DR/SRS that preserves uncertainty as assumptions/open questions or justified N/A values and does not fabricate owners, architecture, targets, compliance outcomes, or rollout decisions.
expectations: Keeps metadata.status as draft.
Makes missing ownership, scope, architecture, compliance, NFR, and delivery decisions visible.
Does not invent metrics, components, owners, or approval outcomes.
Uses N/A only with an explicit confirmed reason.
Continues drafting on non-blocking unknowns and batches questions instead of stalling the draft.

evals.name: accepted-rfc-requires-propagation
evals.prompt: Update the existing DR/SRS at design-review-rfc.md after RFC-07 was accepted to replace synchronous notifications with an event. The RFC page is linked, but its decision has not yet been propagated into the DR/SRS. Keep the operational document honest and identify the propagation work instead of silently treating the RFC as the current design.
evals.expected_output: The DR/SRS does not silently apply the RFC. It records the missing propagation, preserves the current operational behavior, and identifies affected contracts, Use Cases, tests, and backlog as follow-up work.
expectations: Treats the existing DR/SRS as the operational source of truth.
Does not apply RFC-07 behavior before propagation.
Records RFC-07 and the propagation gap in the decision/open-question area.
Identifies affected contracts and downstream artifacts without generating their implementation.

evals.name: use-case-catalog-link-first-and-readiness
evals.prompt: Author a new DR/SRS from the linked PRD at prd.md. Add UC-01 "Upload signed agreement" to the Use Case catalog; its child document is uc-01-upload-signed-agreement.md. Keep the DR/SRS as catalog only and link the child. Then assess whether the child is ready for a backlog agent: it has a trigger and a main flow but no binary acceptance check.
evals.expected_output: A new DR/SRS from the PRD whose Use Case catalog row is only ID, title, and child link, with no detailed body; the child is draft because a binary acceptance check is missing, with a gap and owner, while metadata.status stays draft.
expectations: The catalog row contains only UC-01, its title, and the child link.
No trigger, flow, edge case, postcondition, or acceptance-check body appears in the DR/SRS.
Reports the child as draft, not ready, because the binary acceptance check is missing, and does not invent one.
Keeps metadata.status as draft and does not force the document review gate.

evals.name: backlog-handoff-with-declared-gaps
evals.prompt: Use the day-zero PRD at prd.md, where the sponsor, owner, and thresholds are still TBD, plus the ready Use Case child at uc-01-upload-signed-agreement-ready.md. The child has a trigger, a main flow, AC-01, a priority, and its processing component (solution.components.item-001) and upload contract (contracts.item-001). Produce the DR/SRS catalog and decide what a backlog agent can consume now. Do not invent the missing sponsor, owner, or thresholds.
evals.expected_output: A draft DR/SRS that declares the PRD gaps but still lists UC-01 with its child link; the child is ready because it meets the minimum core and names its component and contract, and handoff does not require the document review gate.
expectations: Keeps metadata.status as draft while the UC-01 child is ready.
Lists UC-01 in the catalog with only ID, title, and child link.
Leaves the component, contract, priority, and status references in the child page, not in the DR catalog.
Keeps sponsor, owner, and threshold gaps visible with owners instead of inventing values.
States that backlog generation consumes ready children without requiring metadata.status: review.

evals.name: direct-intake-without-prd
evals.prompt: Crea una Design Review / SRS per un'iniziativa di hardening infrastrutturale. Non esiste un PRD né materiale di discovery: l'intake è una lista di attività: ruotare le credenziali del database, imporre mTLS tra i servizi interni e aggiungere un alert sulla scadenza dei certificati. Metti outcome e scope nella DR/SRS, lascia il JTBD collegato come non applicabile e non inventare un'esigenza di prodotto né bloccare il documento per l'assenza del PRD. Scrivi Markdown in design-review.md.
evals.expected_output: A DR/SRS whose visible content is in Italian, with references.prd marked N/A — direct DR/SRS intake, the initiative outcome and scope placed in the Expected outcome section, Use Case catalog entries with linked JTBD N/A on their child pages, and no fabricated product need, KPI, or guardrail.
expectations: Writes visible content in Italian (session language) while keeping IDs and machine-facing values unchanged.
Marks references.prd as N/A — direct DR/SRS intake and satisfies ready.prd via outcome/scope in the DR/SRS.
Keeps the catalog to ID, title, and child link, with linked JTBD = N/A — no linked PRD on the child.
Does not block the draft and does not fabricate product need, KPIs, or guardrails.

evals.name: stable-identifiers-and-change-propagation
evals.prompt: Normalize identifiers and handle two change situations. Two source documents both label different behaviors as UC-03 in the DR/SRS. The linked PRD is "PRD-pagamenti" and defines JTBD-01; note that PRD and JTBD are optional and may be absent entirely. (A) Pre-baseline, two sources contradict each other on the retention period. (B) The baseline is approved and a new decision materially changes the API response contract. Add a cross-cutting availability target and an API acceptance check for UC-05. Record outcomes in the open questions/decisions area.
evals.expected_output: The duplicate UC-03 is flagged as possible-duplicate/gap without renumbering; identifiers follow the canonical namespaces (PRD-pagamenti/JTBD-01, NFR-XX, AC-UC-05-YY); the pre-baseline contradiction becomes an open question/gap, not a Change Request; the post-baseline material change becomes a Change Request with propagation to contracts, Use Cases, and tests, without implementing it.
expectations: Flags the duplicate UC-03 as possible-duplicate/gap and never renumbers or reuses an ID.
Uses canonical ID namespaces (NFR-XX, AC-UC-XX-YY, PRD-xxx/JTBD-yy) and tolerates absent PRD/JTBD (N/A).
Pre-baseline contradiction produces an open question/gap, not a Change Request.
Post-baseline material change to the API contract produces a Change Request with propagation to contracts, Use Cases, and tests, without implementing it.

evals.name: use-case-detail-stays-in-child
evals.prompt: The DR/SRS at design-review-rfc.md is the parent. A UC-03 child document for "Emit payment outcome event" references component solution.context.item-001 and contract contracts.item-001, and carries status ready. Add UC-03 to the parent catalog. Keep the parent link-first and do not duplicate the child's detail.
evals.expected_output: The UC-03 catalog row is only ID, title, and child link; component, contract, status, and behavior stay in the child; existing IDs are unchanged.
expectations: Adds a UC-03 catalog row containing only its ID, title, and child link.
Does not copy the component, contract, status, priority, or behavior into the catalog.
Keeps the child page as the home of the component and contract references.
Preserves the existing catalog IDs without renumbering.

evals.name: new-use-case-emerges-after-baseline
evals.prompt: The DR/SRS baseline is approved. During implementation a new Use Case emerges inside the agreed scope, and an existing Use Case that already has Jira items gains a more detailed acceptance check without changing observable behavior. Handle both. Do not create a Change Request for detail inside the agreed scope, and do not renumber existing entries.
evals.expected_output: The new Use Case takes the next free UC-XX ID and a child page; the detail-only acceptance change is a normal update; only a material behavior, scope, or contract change is a Change Request; the changed Use Case with existing Jira items is flagged for synchronization.
expectations: Allocates the next free UC-XX ID and never renumbers existing Use Cases.
Treats the detail-only acceptance change as a normal update, not a Change Request.
Flags the changed Use Case with existing Jira items for synchronization.
Keeps material behavior/scope/contract changes as the only Change Request trigger.

evals.name: minimal-dr-section-labels
evals.prompt: Create a minimal DR/SRS for a small internal tooling change from a task-centric intake with no PRD and no external interfaces. Follow the template section labels: fill every Always section, mark If applicable sections N/A with a confirmed reason, and omit Optional sections. Confirm a backlog agent can consume the result.
evals.expected_output: A minimal DR/SRS that fills only the Always sections, marks the non-applicable If applicable sections N/A with reasons, omits Optional sections, and shows the backlog handoff path without forcing metadata.status: review.
expectations: Fills every Always section and does not leave Always placeholders unresolved.
Marks each non-applicable If applicable section N/A — <confirmed reason>.
Omits Optional sections or keeps them minimal and justified.
Identifies a ready Use Case or an explicit owner gap without requiring the document review gate.
